subject: Post-call: FinTechCo logging/redaction requirements & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@fintechco.com>, Thomas Reynolds <t.reynolds@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: FinTechCo logging/redaction requirements & next steps

Hi Alice / Tom,

Thanks again for the time this morning — really helpful to walk through your data handling and compliance needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Recap of requirements we captured:
- Retain request/response logs for 90 days for troubleshooting and auditability, but redact PII (card numbers, SSNs, customer email addresses) before long-term storage.
- Ability to scrub/strip HTTP headers that may carry sensitive values (Authorization, X-Trace-Id, X-Session).
- Trace/Correlation IDs: you need the ability to correlate requests for debugging, but IDs must be anonymized or reversible only with your key.
- Data residency: logs must be stored in US regions for production data.
- SOC 2 and evidence: you requested our SOC 2 report and details on logging controls.

What Redwood can offer (high-level):
- Runtime redaction: configurable masking/regex rules to redact sensitive tokens in both request payloads and model responses before logs are written.
- Header scrubbing: per-route header allowlists/blocklists.
- Trace id handling: option to hash trace IDs server-side (deterministic hashing) or to replace with a derived correlation token scoped to your tenant; we can also send trace copies to customer-managed logging endpoints if preferred.
- Retention controls: per-account retention policies (30/90/365 days) with automated deletion and export hooks.
- Private deployment + KMS: for stricter isolation and key control, we can offer a Private deployment behind your VPC with customer-managed KMS for any reversible mapping keys.

Attachments I’m including: redaction-controls-overview.pdf (high-level options) and a small sample-logs.jsonl showing masked vs unmasked examples.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with our platform team to validate regex/structured-redaction approach and show a demo (30–45m) — can you share a couple of windows this week?
2) You provide a couple of representative sample logs (sanitized) or schemas so we can validate masking rules against real payload shapes.
3) I’ll send SOC 2 and a short write-up on our retention + deletion controls.

If that looks right, I’ll schedule the deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

On Mon, Aug 15, 2027 at 09:47 AM Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@fintechco.com> wrote:
> Thanks for sending over the notes from the discovery call. A couple clarifications before we book the deep-dive:
>
> - Redaction scope: we need card PAN masking (keep first 6 / last 4 masked if stored), SSN removal, and email hashing. We also need to ensure model outputs never echo PII back into logs.
> - Trace IDs: we do need correlation IDs for incident investigations, but they must not be raw user identifiers. Can REDWOOD support hashing the trace ID using our key or produce a reversible token only our security team can decode?
> - Retention: 90 days is our default for logs but we may need longer for certain audit windows. Can retention be set per-route?
>
> Appreciate the attachments. Looking forward to the SOC 2 and the sample config.
>
> Best,
> Alice
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Thomas Reynolds <t.reynolds@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinTechCo logging/redaction requirements & next steps

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A few follow-ups inline: 

> - Runtime redaction: configurable masking/regex rules to redact sensitive tokens in both request payloads and model responses before logs are written.

This is critical. We prefer server-side redaction before any logs leave the runtime. If you offer both structured-field redaction (recommended) and regex fallback, that would work.

> - Trace id handling: option to hash trace IDs server-side (deterministic hashing) or to replace with a derived correlation token scoped to your tenant; we can also send trace copies to customer-managed logging endpoints if preferred.

We want to avoid any reversible mapping stored by Redwood. Deterministic hashing with a customer-provided salt sounds acceptable as long as we can supply the salt or have the hashing occur in our environment (private deployment).

> - Retention controls: per-account retention policies (30/90/365 days) with automated deletion and export hooks.

Per-route retention would be ideal. For example, requests hitting our payments route should default to 90 days; support routes could be shorter. Can your platform support route-level policies?

Also: please share the SOC 2 report and any details about access controls for logs (who at Redwood can view unredacted logs during debug).

Happy to confirm times for the deep-dive — Thurs 8/17 10–11am PT or Fri 8/18 1–2pm PT work for our platform/security folks.

Best,
Alice
--
Alice Johnson
Head of Platform Security | FinTechCo
alice.johnson@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@fintechco.com>, Thomas Reynolds <t.reynolds@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinTechCo logging/redaction requirements & next steps

Alice — thanks for the clarifications, that all makes sense. Quick answers and plan: 

1) Server-side redaction before logs leave the runtime: yes — Redwood supports pre-write hooks that can apply structured-field redaction (preferred) and regex-based masking for free-text fields. We will demo both approaches in the deep-dive.

2) Trace ID handling: two options we’ll demo:
   - Deterministic hashing using a customer-supplied salt (hash stored, original not reversible without salt).
   - Customer KMS-backed reversible mapping in Private deployments (you control keys; Redwood cannot decode).
We will highlight pros/cons in the technical session.

3) Route-level retention: supported. Policies can be configured per-route/model with inheritance at the account level. We’ll show how to set a default 90d but override for payments routes.

4) Access controls: unredacted logs are restricted to a small SRE/Platform admin role and require just-in-time access with an auditorized approval workflow; we’ll include a short section from our SOC 2 report on access control procedures.

Attachments: redaction-controls-overview.pdf and sample-logs.jsonl (sample shows a payments request and the masked output we’d produce).

Proposed next steps (I’ll take action today):
- I’ll get SOC 2 and a short access-control summary to you by EOD.
- Dev — can you put together a 2–3 slide tech summary on the redaction flow (regex + structured) and a sample route-policy snippet? Attach the sample-logs.jsonl as well.
- Naomi — can you confirm availability for the deep-dive slots Alice suggested (Thu 8/17 10am PT or Fri 8/18 1pm PT)?

If those two slots don’t work, I’ll propose alternatives.

Thanks all — looped in Dev and Naomi to action items.

—
Marissa
